cover.alt: Cover of The Basilisk Book with the Basilisk mark above a glowing path through a field of Python type symbols.

figures.title: The journey from first diagnostic to team workflow
figures.alt: A four-stage reading journey from checking one Python call through understanding types, configuring a project, and shipping in CI.

figures.title: One analysis engine, several developer surfaces
figures.alt: Python source and project configuration flow through Basilisk's parser, resolver, and checker to CLI diagnostics and editor language features.

figures.title: Basilisk in a real editor workspace
figures.alt: A clean VS Code workspace showing Basilisk diagnostics, hover information, and the Basilisk activity panel around the Signal Box project.

figures.title: Choose the integration that matches your editor
figures.alt: A decision map routes VS Code-family, Neovim, Zed, and command-line readers to the appropriate Basilisk installation path.

figures.title: Verify the Basilisk binary
figures.alt: A terminal displays the Basilisk version and formatter provenance before the first project check.

figures.title: A default Python-spec error and its clean result
figures.alt: Side-by-side terminal output shows a wrong argument type reported by Basilisk and the same file passing after correction.

figures.title: Anatomy of a Basilisk diagnostic
figures.alt: Numbered callouts identify severity, stable rule identifier, source span, help, note, and website link in a real diagnostic.

figures.title: Hover reveals the inferred contract
figures.alt: An editor hover over a Signal Box function displays its inferred callable signature and source provenance.

figures.title: Observe before you change
figures.alt: A feedback loop moves from source evidence to a type relationship, a deliberate code change, and a repeated Basilisk check.

figures.title: Annotations inform tools without converting values
figures.alt: Two aligned lanes separate a Python value's runtime behavior from the static information an annotation gives Basilisk.

figures.title: A union describes several permitted possibilities
figures.alt: Example string, float, and None values enter one union-typed boundary while unrelated values stop outside it.

figures.title: Any removes information in both directions
figures.alt: A precise type trace becomes an unlabelled channel at Any, illustrating why later operations carry less useful static evidence.

figures.title: Can this value be used here?
figures.alt: Values approach a labelled destination type; compatible values pass through while an incompatible value produces a diagnostic.

figures.title: Parameters receive and returns promise
figures.alt: A function contract connects typed argument ports to a body and a typed return port with concrete Signal Box values.

figures.title: Mutation changes the compatibility question
figures.alt: The same mutable list is read and written through two type views, exposing the unsafe write that prevents a tempting substitution.

figures.title: Each branch carries more specific information
figures.alt: A broad reading union splits across None, numeric, and error branches, with the remaining type labelled on every path.

figures.title: A TypeGuard gives a checker-readable positive test
figures.alt: A user-defined predicate checks dictionary evidence and narrows the true branch to the SignalReading TypedDict.

figures.title: A missing case leaves a visible path
figures.alt: A real Basilisk match diagnostic points to an unhandled alert variant, followed by a clean exhaustive match.

figures.title: External shape in, domain model out
figures.alt: A dictionary-shaped external reading is validated and transformed into a dataclass before reaching the core application.

figures.title: Choose a structure that matches the boundary
figures.alt: The same reading fields appear as a TypedDict, dataclass, named tuple, and ordinary class with their relevant differences highlighted.

figures.title: One container preserves different payload types
figures.alt: A generic page container keeps its reading payload type as concrete examples substitute different type arguments.

figures.title: Overloads connect inputs to precise outputs
figures.alt: Two documented call shapes map to distinct return types while sharing one implementation body.

figures.title: Basilisk searches type information in order
figures.alt: Stacked search layers show project stub overrides, source packages, standard-library typeshed information, and installed typed packages.

figures.title: Hover shows where an imported signature came from
figures.alt: An editor hover identifies whether a sensor package signature came from source, a local stub, or a typeshed source.

figures.title: Generate, inspect, narrow, and maintain a local stub
figures.alt: A package without type information moves through stub generation, human review, project override, and a successful re-check.

figures.title: Configuration becomes a rule decision for one file
figures.alt: Project settings, individual rule severity, path override, and inline directive resolve to one effective diagnostic severity.

figures.title: Browse and preview rules in the configuration editor
figures.alt: The real VS Code configuration editor shows Python-spec and opt-in Basilisk rules with an explicit severity preview.

figures.title: The same rule can express different path policy
figures.alt: Two files under source and vendor paths show different effective severities produced by a deliberate per-path override.

figures.title: Reduce high-confidence work before adopting the remainder
figures.alt: An initial diagnostic set passes through safe fixes and review before the remaining files enter an explicit adopted-warning state.

figures.title: Preview the work a safe fix actually performed
figures.alt: A terminal and source diff show a bounded Basilisk fix followed by diagnostics that still require a human decision.

figures.title: Adopted work remains visible
figures.alt: Basilisk adoption status lists migrated and remaining Signal Box files without removing their diagnostics from the workflow.

figures.title: The editor asks; Basilisk answers from shared analysis
figures.alt: Editor requests for hover, completion, navigation, and rename loop through one Basilisk language-server workspace state.

figures.title: Keep the contract in view while editing
figures.alt: A compact editor crop combines function completion, signature help, and hover around a Signal Box call site.

figures.title: Preview a rename across modules
figures.alt: A real rename preview lists references in several Signal Box modules before any workspace edit is accepted.

figures.title: A quick fix is a proposed edit
figures.alt: The editor lightbulb and diff preview show a narrow Basilisk code action while leaving a separate type decision untouched.

figures.title: Static checks, tests, debugging, and profiling answer different questions
figures.alt: Four connected evidence lanes show Basilisk checking compatibility, tests checking examples, debugging inspecting state, and profiling measuring execution.

figures.title: Discover and run the Signal Box tests
figures.alt: The editor Test Explorer displays discovered Signal Box tests and a selected passing result with source navigation.

figures.title: Pause where the static model meets runtime state
figures.alt: A real VS Code debug session pauses in Signal Box with the relevant variables, call stack, and current source line visible.

figures.title: Measure a hot path before changing it
figures.alt: Basilisk CPU profiling shows source heat annotations and a flame graph that identify the Signal Box aggregation hot path.

figures.title: Run the same verified check in CI
figures.alt: A clean CI terminal capture shows the pinned Basilisk version, project-root check, test result, and successful process status.
